    18    This is defined as the supremum of the cardinalities of linearly independent subsets.

    21

    24  * `LinearMap.rank_le_of_surjective`: the target of a surjective linear map has dimension

    26  
    27  ## Implementation notes
    28  
    29  Many theorems in this file are not universe-generic when they relate dimensions
    30  in different universes. They should be as general as they can be without
    31  inserting `lift`s. The types `M`, `M'`, ... all live in different universes,
    32  and `M₁`, `M₂`, ... all live in the same universe.

    53  /-- The rank of a module, defined as a term of type `Cardinal`.
    54  
    55  We define this as the supremum of the cardinalities of linearly independent subsets.
    56  The supremum may not be attained, see https://mathoverflow.net/a/263053.
    57  
    58  For a free module over any ring satisfying the strong rank condition
    59  (e.g. left-Noetherian rings, commutative rings, and in particular division rings and fields),
    60  this is the same as the dimension of the space (i.e. the cardinality of any basis).
    61  
    62  In particular this agrees with the usual notion of the dimension of a vector space.
